description: Output report schema for AIFA style consultation. Single source of truth — prompt and frontend both reference this file. Defines exact sections the LLM must produce.

report_sections.title: Your Style Profile
report_sections.content: 2-3 sentence summary of user's body type, key features, and what this means for their style. Written in second person ('You have...'). Mention the 1-2 most impactful body traits.
report_sections.example: You have a heavy build at 5'5" with a wide face and short neck. This means your best looks will focus on creating vertical lines and keeping things streamlined — no clutter, no tight fits, just clean and confident.

report_sections.title: Your Golden Rules
report_sections.content: 3-5 most impactful style principles specific to this user's body. Not generic advice — derived from their specific conflicts and top-scoring patterns. Numbered list.
example_rules: V-necklines always — they elongate your torso and open up your neck
Regular fit is your sweet spot — room without drowning in fabric
Dark colors from waist down — slimming and elongating

report_sections.title: T-Shirts
report_sections.content: Best fit + neckline + sleeve + fabric weight. Top 2-3 picks with brief reason. What to avoid with brief reason. Written conversationally.
report_sections.format: For each subsection: top picks (score 7+) with one-line reason, then 'avoid' items (score 1-4) with one-line reason. Skip items scored 5-6 unless relevant.

report_sections.title: Polos
report_sections.content: Best fit + collar + fabric. Same format as tshirts.

report_sections.title: Casual Shirts
report_sections.content: Best types + fit + collar + fabric. Same format.

report_sections.title: Jeans
report_sections.content: Best fit + wash + rise + stretch + leg shape. Critical category — most users wear jeans daily.

report_sections.title: Jackets & Layers
report_sections.content: OPTIONAL section. Only include if style_track warrants it. Mark as 'optional add-ons'. Best jacket types + hoodie subtypes + weight guidance.
report_sections.note: Always frame as optional: 'When you need a layer...' not 'You should wear...'

report_sections.title: Casual Shoes
report_sections.content: Best casual shoe types + boot types (if applicable). Include formality level guidance.

report_sections.title: Sandals
report_sections.content: Best sandal types + when to wear them.

report_sections.title: Your Fabric & Texture Strategy
report_sections.content: Body-type-specific fabric and texture advice. Covers: which fabric weights suit this build, which textures work (slim → textured fabrics add bulk; heavy → smooth structured fabrics minimize), specific fabric picks per garment type (GSM for tees, pique vs jersey for polos, etc.).

report_sections.title: Your Color Playbook
report_sections.content: 3 subsections: (1) Colors that make you look great (near face), (2) Safe bottom/footwear colors, (3) Colors to avoid. Include metal recommendation (gold/silver). Based on undertone + contrast + Indian skin profile.

report_sections.title: What to Avoid
report_sections.content: Consolidated list of items scored 1-4 across all categories. Grouped by garment type. Each with one-line reason. This is the 'never do this' section.
report_sections.format: Bullet list. Keep it punchy: 'Skinny jeans — accentuates width contrast, creates stuffed look'

report_sections.title: Outfit Ideas That Work for You
report_sections.content: 6-8 complete outfit combinations personalized for this user. Each outfit has: name, all pieces (top + bottom + footwear + optional layer), color suggestion, and 1-sentence 'why it works for you'. Derived from templates + pairings + body scores. Every piece must be scored 7+ for this user.

outfit_format.name: Descriptive name (e.g., 'Weekend Errand Run')
outfit_format.why: One sentence connecting to their body type advantage

report_sections.title: Tailoring Tips
report_sections.content: Practical Indian-specific tailoring advice. What to get tailored (taper jeans, shorten sleeves, take in shirt waist), what NOT to tailor (shoulders, overall size). Reference local darzi culture and Rs 50-200 cost. Highest-ROI style advice for Indian men on any budget.

report_sections.title: Your Shopping Starter Kit
report_sections.content: Top 10 items to buy first, in priority order. Each item is specific with garment type, fit, color, and fabric: 'Navy V-neck regular fit tee in midweight cotton' not just 'a tee'. Based on highest scores + most versatile pairings. No brands, no stores, no prices.
report_sections.format: Numbered 1-10. Each: item name (type + fit + color + fabric) + why it's priority

formatting_rules.tone: friendly, practical, like a knowledgeable friend — not a textbook

9-10.label: best
9-10.language: your best bet, go for this confidently, this is made for you

7-8.label: great
7-8.language: works great, solid choice, can't go wrong with this

5-6.label: okay
5-6.language: acceptable but not ideal, works in a pinch, not your strongest look

3-4.label: caution
3-4.language: generally avoid, not your best look, proceed with caution

1-2.label: avoid
1-2.language: DO NOT mention as recommendation. Only list in 'avoid' section with reason.

priority_hierarchy: 1. Body scores (build, height, face, neck) — highest authority
2. Conflict resolutions — must be reflected in all recommendations
3. Color palette — determines color suggestions in outfits
5. Template guidance — starting points for outfit ideas
6. RAG knowledge — provides reasoning for explanations
